subject: science
domain: From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes
intro: Living things are built largely from carbon-based molecules. The sugars made in photosynthesis contain carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen. Organisms use these atoms, sometimes adding other elements like nitrogen, to build larger molecules. For example, adding nitrogen lets cells build amino acids, which join to form proteins. Carbon atoms can link into long chains and rings, so they can form many large molecules such as carbohydrates, proteins, and fats. In this way, the atoms from sugar become the building blocks of an organism's body.

items.prompt: Sugar molecules contain carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen. What element must be added to build amino acids, which make proteins?

steps: Amino acids contain carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen like sugar, but also one more element.
So nitrogen must be added to the atoms from sugar to build amino acids.
solution.answer: Nitrogen must be added to the carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen to build amino acids.

items.prompt: Why is carbon able to form so many different large molecules in living things?

steps: Carbon atoms can bond to several other atoms at once.
This lets carbon link into long chains and rings.
Because of this, carbon can form many different large molecules like carbohydrates, proteins, and fats.
solution.answer: Carbon can bond to several atoms and form long chains and rings, so it can build many different large molecules.

items.prompt: How do atoms from the sugar made in photosynthesis end up as part of an organism's body?

steps: Sugar provides carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen atoms.
Organisms rearrange these atoms, adding other elements, to build larger molecules like proteins and fats.
These molecules make up the organism's body, so sugar atoms become body material.
solution.answer: The carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen from sugar are rearranged, with other elements added, into larger molecules that build the body.

items.prompt: Name one large carbon-based molecule found in living things.

steps: Living things are built from large carbon-based molecules.
Examples include proteins, carbohydrates, and fats.

items.prompt: Amino acids join together to form what kind of large molecule?

steps: Amino acids are the building blocks of a certain molecule.
Many amino acids join to form proteins.

items.prompt: Construct an explanation for how a plant uses sugar to build a protein.

steps: The sugar provides carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen atoms.
The plant adds nitrogen to build amino acids from these atoms.
The amino acids then join together to form a protein, so sugar plus nitrogen builds proteins.
solution.answer: The plant uses carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen from sugar, adds nitrogen to make amino acids, and joins the amino acids into a protein.
